specification.title: Savepoint recovery: roll back the failing statement, then commit
steps: Start a transaction with the framework's ordinary transaction API.
Write the marker `tx` and make sure the write was sent.
Establish a savepoint with the framework's supported savepoint or nested-transaction API.
Insert the duplicate value 'taken' inside that savepoint. After the unique violation, roll back to the savepoint using that API.
Checkpoint `before-end`: report the same backend PID. Send no query.
Commit the surrounding transaction through the ordinary API.
Checkpoint `after-api` as soon as that API has returned, before any reuse.
Run one new transaction that writes `reuse`. Checkpoint `reuse-after-write` if it starts.
Checkpoint `after-end`, as soon as the case function has returned.

invariants.statement: The run recorded the application-visible outcome and an independent database outcome that agree with each other. This invariant does not judge whether the application-visible outcome was the correct commit report. That judgment is in the research summary.

execution.description: HikariCP 7.1.0 with maximumPoolSize 1. No other pool setting is changed. Between the two units the connection is released through Spring's normal path. The pool is not closed, the connection is not evicted, and no validation query is issued between them. TX-03 runs only in this mode.
execution.form: TransactionTemplate.execute with a PROPAGATION_NESTED template around the duplicate. The nested error is contained and the outer callback returns.

server.version: PostgreSQL 18.6 (Debian 18.6-1.pgdg13+2) on aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu, compiled by gcc (Debian 14.2.0-19) 14.2.0, 64-bit

fault.mechanism: A unique_violation raised by PostgreSQL inside a savepoint. The application rolls back to that savepoint and commits the outer transaction. No statement is withheld or rewritten.
fault.injection_point: Inside the savepoint, after the outer write.
fault.expected_server: ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT undoes the failed statement. The outer COMMIT can commit the earlier write.
fault.expected_client: The application uses the framework's savepoint API to recover, then commits.

knowledge: A committed outer transaction after a rolled-back savepoint is a successful recovery, not a commit of an aborted transaction.

api_outcome.basis: TransactionTemplate.execute returned normally, so the template committed
api_outcome.contract: Spring Framework 7.0.9 TransactionTemplate.execute (org.springframework.transaction.support.TransactionTemplate) calls PlatformTransactionManager.commit only when the callback returns, and on a RuntimeException or Error it rolls the transaction back and rethrows that same throwable. The 7.0.9 reference, Rolling Back a Declarative Transaction, states the default rule: "In its default configuration, the Spring Framework's transaction infrastructure code marks a transaction for rollback only in the case of runtime, unchecked exceptions. That is, when the thrown exception is an instance or subclass of RuntimeException. (Error instances also, by default, result in a rollback)." The default tx:advice settings say: "Any RuntimeException triggers rollback, and any checked Exception does not." No custom rollback rule is installed. The nested TransactionTemplate uses PROPAGATION_NESTED. The 7.0.9 reference, Understanding PROPAGATION_NESTED, states: "PROPAGATION_NESTED uses a single physical transaction with multiple savepoints that it can roll back to. Such partial rollbacks let an inner transaction scope trigger a rollback for its scope, with the outer transaction being able to continue the physical transaction despite some operations having been rolled back. This setting is typically mapped onto JDBC savepoints, so it works only with JDBC resource transactions." DataSourceTransactionManager's class javadoc states: "This transaction manager supports nested transactions via the JDBC Savepoint mechanism."

violation.message: PreparedStatementCallback; SQL [insert into uniq (code) values (?)]; ERROR: duplicate key value violates unique constraint "uniq_code_key" Detail: Key (code)=(taken) already exists.

evaluation.mechanism_detail: at before-end the session was "idle in transaction"; at after-api the session was "idle" and its last statement was "COMMIT"
evaluation.reason: PR-01.1 held: the API reported committed; at before-end the session was "idle in transaction"; at after-api the session was "idle" and its last statement was "COMMIT"

a unique_violation (23505) was observed on the failing statement
the marker visibility agrees with pg_xact_status() for the captured transaction
